newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lockheed Martin seeks growth in aircaft services.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed Martin seeks growth in aircaft services.

text.p: Lockheed Martin plans to expand activities in aircraft service and support, the president and chief operating officer of the U.S. aerospace group's aeronautics sector told Reuters.

James Blackwell said at the Paris air show that four companies grouped in the services area generate annual turnover of around $800 million and he wants to see that grow by eight to 10 percent. He gave no timetable.

Lockheed Martin's move into services echoes ambitions by industry titan Boeing, engine maker Pratt & Whitney, a unit of United Technoloies Corp, and conglomerate General Electric, which recently acquired a major aviation services company.
Airlines also compete to provide third-party aircraft maintenance services.

Blackwell declined to detail what margins he was aiming for, other than to say they would be "respectable" and saw "high returns on assets" in this area. The services domain includes activities such as major modifications of aircraft and contract field maintenance.

Lockheed Martin had $27 billion in annual sales, of which the aeronautics sector accounted for "less than $6 billion," Blackwell said. The corporation as a whole aims to generate around 30 percent of turnover from export sales in "the next few years," compared to 18 percent currently, he said.
